pending_commit.commit_message: BACKPORT: tunnels: Don't apply GRO to multiple layers of encapsulation. When drivers express support for TSO of encapsulated packets, they only mean that they can do it for one layer of encapsulation. Supporting additional levels would mean updating, at a minimum, more IP length fields and they are unaware of this. No encapsulation device expresses support for handling offloaded encapsulated packets, so we won't generate these types of frames in the transmit path. However, GRO doesn't have a check for multiple levels of encapsulation and will attempt to build them. UDP tunnel GRO actually does prevent this situation but it only handles multiple UDP tunnels stacked on top of each other. This generalizes that solution to prevent any kind of tunnel stacking that would cause problems. Fixes: bf5a755f ("net-gre-gro: Add GRE support to the GRO stack") Signed-off-by: Jesse Gross <jesse@kernel.org> Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net> (cherry picked from commit fac8e0f579695a3ecbc4d3cac369139d7f819971) Notes on backport: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ The upstream patch doesn't apply cleanly on top of ChromeOS 3.14 kernel. - In 3.14, `struct napi_gro_cb' defined in include/linux/netdevice.h doesn't store its `udp_mark' field as bit field, so we simply rename `udp_mark' to `encap_mark' like the upstream patch does. - net/ipv4/af_net.c is left unchanged as `ipip_offload' defined there doesn't override .gro_receive field. - net/ipv6/ip6_offload.c is left unchanged as `sit_offload' defined there doesn't override .gro_receive field. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ BUG=b:32515955, chromium:672642 TEST=Trybot runs on paladin and release builders. Change-Id: I33a0cd7d9fadd1b85086ded6eff0544846fe3180 Signed-off-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/419806 Reviewed-by: Jorge Lucangeli Obes <jorgelo@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kevin Cernekee <cernekee@chromium.org>

BACKPORT: net: add recursion limit to GRO Currently, GRO can do unlimited recursion through the gro_receive handlers. This was fixed for tunneling protocols by limiting tunnel GRO to one level with encap_mark, but both VLAN and TEB still have this problem. Thus, the kernel is vulnerable to a stack overflow, if we receive a packet composed entirely of VLAN headers. This patch adds a recursion counter to the GRO layer to prevent stack overflow. When a gro_receive function hits the recursion limit, GRO is aborted for this skb and it is processed normally. This recursion counter is put in the GRO CB, but could be turned into a percpu counter if we run out of space in the CB. Thanks to Vladimr Bene <vbenes@redhat.com> for the initial bug report. Fixes: CVE-2016-7039 Fixes: 9b174d88c257 ("net: Add Transparent Ethernet Bridging GRO support.") Fixes: 66e5133f19e9 ("vlan: Add GRO support for non hardware accelerated vlan") Signed-off-by: Sabrina Dubroca <sd@queasysnail.net> Reviewed-by: Jiri Benc <jbenc@redhat.com> Acked-by: Hannes Frederic Sowa <hannes@stressinduktion.org> Acked-by: Tom Herbert <tom@herbertland.com> Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net> (cherry picked from commit fcd91dd449867c6bfe56a81cabba76b829fd05cd) Notes on backport: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ The upstream patch doesn't apply cleanly on top of ChromeOS 3.14 kernel. - In 3.18, `struct napi_gro_cb' defined in include/linux/netdevice.h doesn't store its fields as bit field, so we simply add `recursion_counter' field as a full u8 field. - The call_gro_receive change doesn't apply to the following files as either the file doesn't exist or no call to .gro_receive exists in the code yet. drivers/net/geneve.c net/8021q/vlan.c net/ethernet/eth.c net/ipv4/fou.c - call_gro_receive is used instead of call_gro_receive_sk in net/ipv4/udp_offload.c as the .gro_receive callback doesn't take `struct sk` argument. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ BUG=b:32515955, chromium:672642 TEST=Trybot runs on paladin and release builders. CHROMIUM: tegra: host: fix possible overflow with num_syncpt_incrs num_syncpt_incrs is signed in channel submit ioctl. This means userspace can assign a negative value to it then bypass all checkings in channel submit. This might bring several security issues like stack corruption/kernel crash. This patch is inspired by a security report here: http://nvidia.custhelp.com/app/answers/detail/a_id/4276 Change-Id: I3f7787cbda7c66c3904e80e8f47dbe5df0c889df Signed-off-by: Mark Zhang <markz@gpartner-nvidia.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/420104 Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: tegra: host: fix integer overflow Below addition on 32 bit architecture machines could cause integer overflow since we will assign overflowed value to "num_unpins" s64 num_unpins = num_cmdbufs + num_relocs Fix this and other calculations by explicitly typecasting variables to u64 first. This patch is inspired by a security report here: http://nvidia.custhelp.com/app/answers/detail/a_id/4276 Change-Id: Id43c4c68c13d6f473c116d5b29b5652182d7d12a Signed-off-by: Deepak Nibade <dnibade@nvidia.com> Signed-off-by: Mark Zhang <markz@gpartner-nvidia.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/420105 Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org>

tcpm: fusb302: Don't mistake meaningful packets for GOOD_CRC If a partner port sends a packet at approximately the same time as we send a packet, we may end up with the initial packet followed by the GOOD_CRC reply in our HW FIFO. Don't automatically discard the first packet in the FIFO. Instead, discard the packet only if it's a GOOD_CRC packet. And, modify our get_message function to automatically discard GOOD_CRC in search of a meaningful packet. In addition, due to interrupt latency, we can't rely on receiving one interrupt per incoming packet. If our Rx FIFO is non-empty, assume that it contains at least one packet. BUG=chrome-os-partner:60242 BRANCH=gru TEST=Manual on kevin, attach Apple dongle with no inputs. Attach zinger, verify we negotiate to ~20V. Repeat 10x and verify negotiation is successful each time. CHROMIUM: drm/cirrus: hardcode vram size There is no reliable way of detecting actual VRAM size, which is important in the case of cirrus because cursor data is always stored in the last 16K of VRAM. Because qemu effectivaly hardcodes 4MB but reports 32MB, we hardcode 4MB in the cirrus driver to ensure the cursor works properly.
